findings.title: Mock registered under only one provider id; test will break if default provider changes
findings.rationale: The test overrides only the `openrouter` provider id in `llm`. The tested path (`resolveFeatureModel` when no workspace override exists) picks the registry’s current default provider. If that default changes (e.g. to `openai` or `anthropic`), the mock is missed and the real API is called, making the test flaky and potentially costly. The established pattern in `server/test/conventions.it.test.ts` registers the mock under all three provider ids (`openai`, `anthropic`, `openrouter`).

matched_title: Mock only one LLM provider ID, violating the house rule for model-resolution tests

findings.title: Mock only one LLM provider ID, violating the house rule for model-resolution tests
findings.rationale: The test exercises a code path that resolves its model through `resolveFeatureModel` when no workspace override is saved, but registers a `MockLLMProvider` only under the `openrouter` key. If the registry default is later changed to `openai` or `anthropic`, the mock won't be found and the test will invoke a real, paid API, potentially causing flaky failures, unbilled costs, or assertions against live model output. The repository's house rule explicitly requires registering the mock under all three provider IDs (`openai`, `anthropic`, `openrouter`) to prevent this, as happened previously (commit `f5323f7`).

matched_title: Mock registered under only one provider; will break if registry default changes

findings.title: Mock registered under only one provider; will break if registry default changes
findings.rationale: The test registers a mock LLM provider only under the `openrouter` provider id. However, the code path under test uses `resolveFeatureModel` (see `server/src/modules/settings/feature-models.ts:51` and `server/src/modules/conventions/routes.ts:23`), which resolves the model via the registry default. If the registry default ever moves to a different provider (e.g., `openai` or `anthropic`), the call will bypass the mock and either hit a real, paid API (if credentials exist) or fail with a network error. This voids the test’s guarantee and matches a prior incident (commit f5323f7). Following the repository’s established pattern in `server/test/conventions.it.test.ts:85-90`, the mock should be registered under _all_ provider ids — `openai`, `anthropic`, and `openrouter`.

findings.title: GROUP BY is not exercised with multiple PRs
findings.rationale: The test title and comment describe testing a `GROUP BY pr_id` aggregate query, but the test only inserts rows for a single PR (`pr.id`).  Because `WHERE eq(t.agentRuns.prId, pr.id)` already filters to one PR, the aggregate returns exactly one row whether or not the query contains a `GROUP BY` clause.  A regression that silently drops the `GROUP BY` (e.g., an accidental change to `SELECT SUM(...) FROM agent_runs` without grouping) would still pass, because the filtered result set only ever produces one row.  To guard against that, the test should insert runs for at least two distinct PRs and assert that the observed row count matches the number of PRs and that each PR’s total is correct.  Without that, the test does not exercise what its name claims.

findings.title: Test does not exercise the actual production query's GROUP BY clause
findings.rationale: The test's query filters by a single PR ID with a WHERE clause and then sums cost_usd. It never uses GROUP BY, so it cannot catch a regression where the production route's GROUP BY clause (e.g. missing a column, wrong grouping) breaks. The comment references the route's raw-SQL aggregate, but the test doesn't actually run that aggregate — it runs a different, simpler query that would pass even if the production GROUP BY were entirely removed.

matched_title: Provider mock registered under only one ID instead of all three

findings.title: Provider mock registered under only one ID instead of all three
findings.rationale: The conventions extractor resolves the model through resolveFeatureModel, which selects the registry default provider. Only the `openrouter` key is mocked; when the default provider changes (e.g., to `openai`), the test silently calls the real LLM API, breaking isolation and risking flaky results or real API charges. The repo's established pattern (conventions.it.test.ts:85-90) registers a mock under all three known ids: openai, anthropic, openrouter.

findings.title: Test silently skips when Docker is unavailable
findings.rationale: `beforeAll` returns early when Docker is unavailable, causing the single `it` block to silently pass without running any assertions. In CI or on a machine without Docker, a real regression would be hidden with no indication. The test should use `it.skipIf` or a proper skip strategy.

findings.title: No coverage of status filtering
findings.rationale: The test inserts only `'done'` runs, so it never exercises the branch where non-`'done'` statuses are (or are not) excluded. If the production query filters by status, this test would not catch a regression that accidentally includes pending/failed runs in the cost sum.

findings.title: Grouping across multiple PRs not tested
findings.rationale: Only one PR is inserted, so the test never checks that `GROUP BY pr_id` correctly separates costs across different PRs. A bug that accidentally sums all runs across all PRs would still pass this test.

findings.title: Test assertion contradicts the column's nullability and does not test the intended feature
findings.rationale: The insert on line 20-22 does not provide a value for `retryCount`, so the column remains NULL (the schema defines no default).  The assertion on line 23 expects `row.retryCount` NOT to be null, which is the opposite of the actual behavior.  The test will fail, but **even if it passed** it would not verify that a valid `retry_count` value round-trips through the database — the stated goal of the PR.  This makes the test both wrong and useless for catching production bugs, e.g. a missing migration or a broken column default.

findings.title: Not a real finding
findings.rationale: No secret leaked. This entry is to satisfy the output schema but is not a separate finding.

findings.title: Test does not actually round‑trip a non‑null retry_count value
findings.rationale: The test is named “is recorded on the run row” and the PR description claims it “tests that the column round‑trips through a real insert/select.”  However, the test body never provides a `retryCount` value, so it cannot verify that a non‑null value is stored and retrieved correctly.  A user or future reviewer could be misled into believing the column’s write/read path is covered.  This is a gap that would allow a bug like the column being unmapped in the Drizzle schema but still present in the database to go undetected.

findings.title: Top‑level await for Docker check may cause startup failures and deviates from repo conventions
findings.rationale: The test uses top-level `await` for `dockerAvailable()`.  This is allowed in ESM, but vitest may not handle top-level await well in all configurations.  Moreover, the `describe.skip` fallback means the test runner will always import and evaluate the top-level await even when Docker is unavailable, potentially causing startup errors.  This pattern is not used elsewhere in the repository (other integration tests use a synchronous `describe` with a condition inside `beforeAll`).

matched_title: Test assertion contradicts column schema and does not test round-trip

findings.title: Test assertion contradicts column schema and does not test round-trip
findings.rationale: The test inserts an `agentRuns` row without providing `retryCount` (so the database stores `NULL`, since the column is nullable and has no default), then asserts `expect(row.retryCount).not.toBeNull()`. This assertion always fails because `retryCount` is indeed `NULL`. The test does **not** verify the column round-trips—it never inserts a value and checks it is preserved. It also asserts an incorrect invariant (non‑null with no default). As written the test cannot pass and provides no guard for the new column's presence or round‑trip behavior. This is a critical gap: the test claims to validate the new feature but is fundamentally broken.

findings.title: Test reimplements production query instead of exercising it
findings.rationale: The test reimplements the SUM(cost_usd) aggregate from scratch instead of exercising the actual production code in routes.ts (or a helper it imports).  It uses its own Drizzle query, not the one the real endpoint runs.  If the production query later adds a WHERE filter (status, tenancy, repo scope) or changes the aggregation (COALESCE, rounding), this test will still pass green while the real feature breaks.  The test should import and call the real function or route handler so it guards what actually ships.

findings.title: Silent skip when Docker unavailable
findings.rationale: The test silently returns early when Docker is unavailable (`if (!pg) return;`), never asserting anything.  While this follows a repo convention, it means the test is effectively dead in environments without Docker and gives false confidence in CI runs that lack Docker.  Using `it.skipIf(!pg)` would make the skip explicit and visible in the test runner output.

matched_title: Test asserts not null on a nullable column that is never set

findings.title: Test asserts not null on a nullable column that is never set
findings.rationale: The column `retry_count` is declared nullable (`integer('retry_count')` without `notNull()` or a `default`). The insert on line 20 omits the column, so the database stores `NULL`. The assertion on line 22 (`expect(row.retryCount).not.toBeNull()`) will therefore always fail, making the test red. The test as written does not guard against anything—it is permanently broken and would block CI for no reason.

matched_title: Test assertion contradicts column nullability — test always fails

findings.title: Test assertion contradicts column nullability — test always fails
findings.rationale: The assertion `expect(row.retryCount).not.toBeNull()` will always fail because the column is **nullable** and the insert does not supply a value for `retryCount`, so it defaults to `null`. The test therefore does **not** verify the round-trip behaviour it claims (*”test that the column round-trips through a real insert/select“*). A correct test should insert a known value (e.g. `0` or `3`) and assert equality. In its current form the test is broken and will red on every run, providing no assurance about the production schema change.

findings.title: Entire feature lacks any tests
findings.rationale: The entire share module is added with 0 test files. Every production path (7 endpoints, raw SQL queries, shell commands via execSync, password hashing with MD5, token generation with Math.random) is completely untested. Any bug or vulnerability — including SQL injection in sql.raw, shell injection in execSync, weak token collisions, or password fingerprint reversibility — will never be caught by automated tests. This is an untested path covering the whole feature.

findings.title: Hardcoded secrets in constants.ts
findings.rationale: The secret `MAINTENANCE_API_TOKEN` is hardcoded in constants.ts:23 in plaintext. Additionally, `SHARE_SIGNING_SECRET` (line 14) is also hardcoded. Hardcoded secrets in the source code allow anyone with access to the repository to misuse them, and they cannot be rotated without a code change.

matched_title: No test for SQL injection defense in `findByToken`

findings.title: No test for SQL injection defense in `findByToken`
findings.rationale: The `findByToken` method interpolates `token` directly into a SQL string via `sql.raw`. No test exists that verifies query safety (e.g., that a malicious token cannot inject SQL). This is an untested path that, if exploited, can leak or corrupt data across workspaces.

findings.title: No test for shell injection defense in `exportDigest`
findings.rationale: `execSync` in `exportDigest` uses string interpolation with `EXPORT_DIR` (a constant) and `digestId` (from URL param). If `digestId` contains shell metacharacters, arbitrary commands can execute. No test passes a malformed `digestId` to confirm the shellout is safe.

findings.title: No test for code injection prevention in `renderTemplate`
findings.rationale: `renderTemplate` uses `new Function(...keys, 'return (' + expr + ');')` to evaluate arbitrary JavaScript expressions found in the digest body. An author with write access could inject code that executes server-side. No test covers this code path, let alone verifies that untrusted expressions are sandboxed or sanitized.

findings.title: No test for password enforcement on shared digest read
findings.rationale: `getSharedDigest` resolves a share by token and renders it without ever checking `row.password_hash`. The password field in `CreateShareBody` is created but never enforced on read — any token holder can access a password-protected digest without providing the password. No test verifies that a password-gated share actually requires the password.

findings.title: No test for path traversal protection in `readExport`
findings.rationale: `readExport` passes `name` directly to `readFileSync(join(EXPORT_DIR, name))`. If `name` contains `../` sequences, an attacker can read arbitrary files under the filesystem. No test attempts a path traversal payload.

findings.title: No test for SSRF protection in `unfurl`
findings.rationale: `unfurl` issues a `fetch` to a URL supplied by the requester with no validation. This can be used for server-side request forgery (SSRF) against internal services (e.g., `localhost`, metadata endpoints). No test supplies an internal IP to confirm it is blocked.

matched_title: Missing authorization check for password-protected shares is completely untested

findings.title: Missing authorization check for password-protected shares is completely untested
findings.rationale: No test verifies that a password-protected share link requires the password on access. The production code's `getSharedDigest` (service.ts:49-59) never reads `password_hash` from the repository and never prompts for or checks a password, so the password gating is entirely missing in the read path. Since no test exists for this path, the missing authorization would ship undetected — this is an untested authorization skip. The repository (repository.ts:22-28) stores the hash, which is a red herring without the read‑side check.

findings.title: SQL injection in every repository method is completely untested
findings.rationale: Every query in `ShareRepository` uses `sql.raw` with direct string interpolation of user‑controlled values (`token`, `sort`, `digestId`, `input.token`, `input.passwordHash`) — a textbook SQL injection vulnerability. No test exists that passes crafted inputs (e.g., a token containing `' OR 1=1--`) to exercises like `findByToken`, `list`, `getDigestBody`, or `insert`. An integration test with real Postgres would detect the injection because it would produce a query error or different result, but no such test is present. The test suite therefore does not establish any SQL safety; the injection would ship undetected, and an attacker could read arbitrary data from any table.

findings.title: No test for XSS risk in dangerouslySetInnerHTML on public share page
findings.rationale: The client component `SharedDigestView` renders user‑supplied HTML via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (line 30). No test verifies that the server‑returned `digest.html` is sanitised before rendering. While the server does its own markdown‑to‑HTML conversion, the client test suite mocks `fetch` and would not catch XSS even if a test existed — but here no test at all covers this component. An untested XSS vector in a public, unauthenticated page is a critical security gap that requires a test to confirm safe rendering.
